problems.reason: Different studies place Dakotaraptor in Dromaeosauridae versus Unenlagiidae/Unenlagiinae, conflicting family assignments.
Both sentences describe the same ulnar papillae/quill knobs on the ulna as feather attachment points.
Both state that adult Dakotaraptor individuals were too heavy to fly.
Sentence discusses a turtle shell (Axestemys splendida) rather than Dakotaraptor itself.
Mentions "calaminae" of large pennaceous feathers without prior definition or context.

notes: - contradiction: "Dakotaraptor was placed in Dromaeosauridae, and a cladistic analysis showed it was the sister taxon of Dromaeosaurus." / "A 2019 study by Hartman et al. recovered a placement of Dakotaraptor in Unenlagiidae." / "Dakotaraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae." / "A 2019 study suggests that Dakotaraptor is likely a member of the subfamily Unenlagiinae.": Different studies place Dakotaraptor in Dromaeosauridae versus Unenlagiidae/Unenlagiinae, conflicting family assignments.
